RECEPTION Dharma from Compassionate Place

Compassionate Gaya, those four words are the name of this method of Repentance.

Because he felt that Maitreya Buddha, filled with compassion and love for the present life and future lives, responded to his dream and taught, he named it like that, true to the truth, and did not dare to change it.

Now I obey the teachings of that Compassionate One because I want to protect the Three Jewels: To make demons invisible, to make arrogant people and arrogant monks subdue themselves; Make people who have not planted good roots grow good roots; Once planted, the good roots will grow; Makes people who often cling to attachments and are infatuated with wrong views to develop the mind to let go of attachments; makes people who like Hinayana not doubt Mahayana; People who love Mahayana give birth to joy in Hinayana.

Furthermore, this method of compassionate repentance is greater than all other good deeds. This Dharma is the refuge of all sentient beings; like the bright sun during the day; like the moon shining at night. This Dharma is the eyes of the practitioner, the teacher, the parent, the brother, the true and good knowledge of the practitioner, who goes together to the ashram.

This method of repentance is closer to relatives than flesh and blood, they follow each other forever, even until death they will not separate. Therefore, this Dharma of repentance should be called the Compassionate Path.

Today, the masses, hidden in body or visible in the ashram, establishing this Dharma of repentance, all have great intentions, because there are twelve great causes and conditions:

Today, the masses of colleagues in the ashram should know why they must take refuge in the Three Jewels.

Because the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have boundless great compassion that transcends the world, have boundless great compassion, comfort the world, and love all sentient beings like red children.

That great compassion is always tireless, always seeking good deeds to benefit all; vow to extinguish the fire of greed, anger, and ignorance for all, and to teach and educate so that all can attain the Supreme Bodhi. If sentient beings do not attain Bodhi. Buddha vowed not to attain Enlightenment, because of that reason, the masses need to take refuge in the Three Jewels.

Furthermore, the Buddhas have more compassion for living beings than parents have for their children.

In the sutras it is taught: "Parents love their children for only one lifetime. Buddha's love for sentient beings is endless. Furthermore, parents see their children being ungrateful and resentful, and their love decreases. Buddha and Bodhisattva love sentient beings, but their hearts are not like that. Seeing sentient beings rebel, the compassion of Buddha and Bodhisattva increases forever."

They also entered the Fire Wheel Hell, the Infinite Hell, and endured immeasurable suffering, on behalf of all sentient beings.

Therefore, you should know that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have more compassion for living beings than parents have for their children. CHAPTER TWO

CUT DOUBT

Today, the masses of colleagues in the ashram listen attentively. Argued that:

Cause and effect influence each other, mutual induction and generation; Such natural morality is not wrong. But regarding the karma of living beings, each person is different, so the retribution is not the same; Whether pure or rough, or noble or lowly, or good, or evil, there are countless differences. If there is a difference, it is unclear what the cause of that difference is. Because it is not clear, doubt and confusion arise. Or say people who diligently practice and keep their precepts pure should live a long life, so why do they die early? The butcher (butcher) should have died early but lived long. Honest people should be rich, but why are they poor? People who are greedy and robbers should be poor and miserable, but why are they rich and prosperous?

Everyone thinks that such a mistake is inevitable. Because we are not clear about what we have done in previous lives, the seeds we have planted are not pure, so today we have such inconsistent results.

The Prajnaparamita Sutra teaches: "If someone reads and recites this sutra and is despised by others, it is because that person had heavy karma in a previous life and deserved to fall into an evil path. Today, thanks to people's disdain, the karma of previous lives is destroyed."

Because sentient beings do not wholeheartedly believe in the Buddha's teachings, they have doubts. Sentient beings are bewitched by ignorance, obscuring their minds, so they give rise to such crazy doubts.

Even sentient beings do not believe: Staying in the three realms is suffering, leaving the three realms is happiness. People who are often passionate about the world think life is fun.

Let's try to ask:

If life is truly happy, why is there a mind that knows happiness in the mind that knows suffering?

Excessive eating and drinking will cause illness: measles rash, cough, asthma, bad breath, ascites, pain, discomfort.

When it comes to clothes, I feel even more miserable. When it's cold, if you get a thin coat, you'll be ungrateful to the person who gave it to you, and your heart will feel miserable.

The sun gets a double coat, fleece, and more suffering. If wearing clothes is fun, why does it cause suffering?

If family is supposed to be happy, we should be happy together forever, happily singing and laughing endlessly, why is it so impermanent, we pass away in the blink of an eye! As soon as it is there, it is not there. Soon it will be dark, cry to heaven and earth, bravely break up! Even sentient beings don't know where they came from? Where do you go when you die? People still cry for the lost, embracing pity, burying each other, going straight to the mountain, clasping hands to say goodbye, for a lifetime, how painful it is! Such things, immeasurable suffering, sentient beings are confused and accept them as happiness.

On the contrary, when causing joy in the world, sentient beings consider it suffering.

Seeing men precepting, eating pickled vegetables, raising their bodies for the day, not wearing silk, accustomed to wearing chalk and wearing bright brown clothes, sentient beings all think that these things are self-mortification and misery, not knowing that doing so is causing liberation and sowing seeds of happiness.

Or seeing people giving alms, maintaining precepts, being patient, diligent, walking, worshiping, and reciting diligently, sentient beings all consider it suffering; Not knowing that doing so is cultivating the mind beyond this world, to be happy.

Occasionally, when I see someone sick or dying, I immediately suspect that this person forces this body and mind to work excessively, all day long without taking a break. Human strength cannot bear it. If the practitioner is not diligent and hard-working, he will not lose his life with such useless work.

Today, the mass of colleagues in the ashram should understand clearly.

Such doubts have countless causes and conditions.

Besides, the seeds of doubt and error cannot be completely eliminated by practicing to escape the three realms of samsara, let alone this ordinary human body. Don't worry about getting rid of it in this life, in the next life there will be more.

The assembly has just practiced together, the road is still long, self-cultivation is ascetic, so based on the Buddha's teachings, following the Dharma to practice, there should be no doubts, and rejection of fatigue.

The Buddhas and Saints, the reason they were able to escape from birth and death and reach the other shore of liberation was because of their good deeds, so they achieved the result of liberation without hindrance and freedom.

We today have not yet separated from birth and death, so even thinking about it is pitiful; How can I still desire to stay in this evil life? Now, fortunately, the four elements have not yet decayed; The five blessings are still intact, come and go leisurely, move freely without any effort to practice, what are you waiting for? In the previous life, I did not see the path; This life is a waste, without realizing anything, so how can we save sentient beings in the next life?

Looking back at my own thoughts, it's truly heartbreaking. Nowadays, the masses should only advise each other to practice diligently. They should not say that they must have some enlightenment information to practice; Because Buddhism is long-lasting, it cannot be done in a day. If we keep waiting for news, then one day and then the next, we will never see the results.

meditate, diligently practice asceticism, a little bit

FEELING IN TEARS

Around October 1961, the Emperor Liang's Repentance translation of this meaning arrived in Hue, and Buddhists in the ancient capital joyfully welcomed the Buddha's relics like pearl water. The Venerable, Abbot of Chau Lam Hue Pagoda and more than sixty lay Buddhists set up an altar to worship at his pagoda. While reciting, suddenly everyone in the ashram burst into tears because they could not stop their emotions. Reading the passages describing the ups and downs of sentient beings immersed in and out of the six paths, suffering all the suffering of reincarnation, my heart was moved with compassion. When I think of myself, and my relatives far and near in the 10 directions who are suffering from damnation and punishment, or feel emotions because of the Buddha's passionate teachings and profound teachings, the whole ashram cannot stop the flow of tears.

After the ashram was completed, the Buddhists asked the Venerable to let them establish "Ban Emperor Liang's Repentance" to make friends to practice together.

Every year, on the day of the monks' summer retreat, or whenever they need to worship, they come together to Chau Lam Pagoda to set up an altar and chant.

INTRODUCTION

Everyone born in this world of Desire, except for those who are completely enlightened, no one can avoid mistakes, caused by the three karmas.

Sins have arisen from three karmas, so people who want to get rid of all sins must of course repent of those three karmas, then their sins will be purified.

Buddha taught: "If there is no method of repentance, none of the Buddhists will be liberated."

Likewise, if it weren't for Emperor Liang's Repentance, Mrs. Hy Thi, the Queen of King Liang, would not have been able to escape the tribulation.

Therefore, this set of Emperor Liang's Repentance has a powerful effect, allowing people's sins to be eliminated and blessings to increase.

Feeling that Venerable Thich Vien Giac's translation is very elaborate, so I would like to introduce a few words to all Buddhists near and far. And hopefully this Emperor Liang's Repentance will be disseminated in the ten directions and will bring common benefit to all; If anyone has faith, follow it.

Careful, HT. THICH THIEN HOA

REPLACE THE PREFACE

According to the preface in the main text, this Emperor Liang's Repentance was edited by Venerable Chi Cong during the reign of King Wu De of China.

Former King Luong Vo De had a most beloved Queen named Hy Thi. Because she was loved by the king, her jealousy increased more and more. Hy Thi was jealous of her concubines, cruel to everyone and slandered the Three Jewels. Everyone in the court and outside the district knows that Mrs. Hy Thi is a "Quai Concubine".

Afterwards, she became seriously ill and the doctors urged her to die. One day, late at night, I was sitting in a quiet palace. King Luong Vo De heard people's miserable cries.(1)

Under the dim light, King Luong Vo De felt cold all over and wanted to run away, but couldn't. The king then asked: "Who are you that you could come in here so late at night, so quiet and so secret?" – Oh Emperor! This is Hy Thi. Because I was so cruel, when I died, I had to become a python. Day and night of suffering, my body was stinky, my scales were crawling with worms, the pain was unbearable. Remembering the old love, I came here hoping to ask the Emperor to find a way to save me. Said then disappeared.

After hearing this, King Luong Vo De felt like he had escaped from a nightmare and his heart ached like a knife! Tomorrow when he returns to court, the king will tell the story to the officials to find a way to save Hy Thi.

Among the mandarins, someone suggested: Please invite Venerable Chi Cong to take care of this matter. Emperor Liang Wu approved. Venerable Chi Cong is a highly enlightened monk at that time. Following the king's request, he immediately summoned famous monks to compose this Dharma and set up an altar to perform the penance ceremony for Queen Hy Thi.

The king worshiped with all his heart and soul. The first few days, people heard a strange, fragrant scent throughout the entire ashram.

The recitation reached the fifth volume, right on the spot, in the air, King Luong Vo De heard Hy Thi's voice. She appeared as a beautiful goddess, spoke in human language, and expressed her gratitude to the Venerable Emperor.

Hy Thi said she escaped disaster and was born in Dao Loi Thien Cung, thanks to the merit of repentance.

WHAT DOES REPENTANCE MEAN?

The sutras teach: - One who repented in the previous period. – The penitent regrets too late.

- Repentance means repenting of the evil deeds you have done, vowing to stop them and not daring to commit them again.

– Repentance is repentance. The evil things that have not been done, I swear to never do again. Please do as many good deeds as you can.

The Sanskrit word is called Repentance, the Chinese translation is Repentance, put both words together and read Repentance. Repentance also has repentance and reasons for repentance.

Repentance means setting up an altar, adorning a Buddha statue, offering flowers and incense, respectfully bowing, sincerely praying for the three karmas as one, and confessing one's sins. May the Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas radiate light, use divine power, and bless practitioners to quickly eliminate karma, quickly escape injustice, and be cleansed of all sins.

The reason for repentance is to repent from the mind. Sins are created by the mind. Sin must be destroyed by the mind. If the mind is empty, the sin will not be. If the mind is destroyed, the mind will also be destroyed. Sin is empty, the mind is destroyed, there is nothing left to repent for. That is true repentance.

After bowing once and reciting a sentence, the practitioner should examine his own mind, destroy all delusions, contemplate the principle of non-birth, and know that sins are caused by causes and conditions, and sins are also destroyed by causes and conditions. Cause and effect are the conditions that create sin and the method of repentance.

Sin does not really exist. Because it doesn't really exist, we can turn sins into blessings, suffering into joy, delusion into enlightenment.

When chanting the Buddha's name, we need to truly understand the meaning of that name. Understand to practice and follow the noble qualities of the Buddhas.

For example, we recite a sentence. "Namo Universal Light Buddha", we must at least understand it roughly like this:

We pay our respects (Namo) to the fully enlightened one (Buddha), full of noble, broad and beautiful virtues (Pho) and boundless wisdom (Light).

In addition, we also need to learn more about our own mind. Our mind also has such noble and beautiful qualities.

Namo – Means taking refuge, paying homage, etc. Universal – Means universal, universal, all-pervading, without limits, beyond time and space, without distinction between us and others. On the contrary, Prussia means connoting the virtues of compassion, joy and forgiveness towards all species, all things, all places, everywhere.

Our mind also has such common qualities. From now on we must live according to the calling of our hearts, not negative but positive, not selfish but altruistic, not angry but compassionate, not greedy but almsgiving, not jealous but joyful and equanimous, not stupid but wise.

Light - Meaning absolute clarity, illuminating all ten directions, penetrating three lifetimes without straying from a single thought. Sinners and the sufferings of sentient beings have been created and will be repaid, since when and where, they are all clear and understood.

Our mind has such a clear mind, from now on, we must act and live according to that clear mind, no longer be ignorant and confused and commit crimes.

Buddha - the fully enlightened one, I pay homage to. Buddha is also a clear, pure mind, full of all good virtues, covering the entire dharma world, outside of time.

Our mind also has enlightenment abilities and qualities like Buddha.

So from now on we must follow the Buddha's example, live wisely, be full of virtue like the Buddha, and not commit crimes anymore.

Roughly like that, follow each name one by one and observe your own mind to repent.

Gradually, the good abilities in our mind will be revealed through repentance, compassion, joy, forgiveness, wisdom, merit, and abundant happiness flowing out like water, for us to enjoy.

People who understand and can do so are people with right views, no longer chasing after external circumstances, no wrong views, taking refuge in ghosts and evil spirits.

People with right view only know how to take refuge, worship, and worship the Buddha in their own mind, listening to the voice of their heart.

Paying homage to one Buddha means paying homage to all the Buddhas of the ten directions. If you worship with a mind of compassion, equality, rationality, and without hindrance, then there is no need to worry that sins will not be eliminated and blessings will not be born.

There are many points worth paying attention to and encouraging, because I have noticed that in many places, such as at An Lac Buddhist temple, at Chau Lam Pagoda, Hue, or at Linh Vu Buddhist temple, Nha Trang, Buddhists nominate people who have clear sounds, recite clearly, making it easy for listeners to understand and develop their minds. These people take turns chanting while the others sit and listen. But do not chant with the chanting tone, but remember this is a way of confessing sins, in front of the Buddha platform, often praying to the Three Jewels for rescue. The passages recounting the crimes must be read clearly, sincerely, and earnestly praying for repentance. Lectures on reason and cause and effect need to be read slowly, clearly divided into sentences, so that the listener can easily understand thanks to the strong and meditative voice followed by the sparse sound of each sentence. Occasionally a bell rings. It is also possible not to play the bell, but to ring the bell rarely so that the listener can follow the meaning and think about the crime, in a majestic and mysterious scene, filled with incense smoke. False thoughts cannot interfere with the sincerity of Buddhists. The warning bell dispels the darkness in the heart, making everyone have a transcendent spirit.

Reading and reciting like that, even though practicing as a group, does nothing to distract the mind. Illiterate people can also realize the meaning, see their own sins, and then develop Bodhi mind to repent on behalf of others in the six paths. During this time, if there is a loudspeaker hanging high and resounding far away, the wicked people will be startled and abandon their illegal acts.

Reading and reciting this way is completely different from reciting sutras. When reciting the sutras, each person has a book, and everyone reads loudly to the sound of the instructor's gong. On the contrary, reciting Emperor Liang's Repentance is no different from monks reciting the Vinaya during Bodhisattva hour. One sat up high and loudly chanted, the others sat silently down to listen. If anyone wants to chant loudly according to their own danger, after the ashram is completed, they can chant alone, it is even more precious. Or everyone can chant loudly to the beat of the gong.

DAM HUYEN'S REPENTANCE

In 1957, Mr. Dam Huyen was 90 years old. He is the biological father of friend Pham At, that is, Uncle Mat, owner of Lien Phat shop, 20 Doc Lap street, Nha Trang. He is sick and old. One day while he was lying down to rest, he suddenly let out three loud screams. Uncle Mat woke up and ran to ask. He said: "Did you hear? Buddha stood outside the window and called Dad, telling Dad that he had sinned against your grandmother, so Buddha hadn't taken him away yet. I need to repent for Dad, tomorrow at exactly seven o'clock in the morning, Buddha will come to pick me up. Remember to go to Hai Duc Pagoda and invite the Elder Master, (that is, Venerable Hai Duc) to pray for Dad.

After he finished speaking, Uncle Mat let his fellow believers know and immediately organized the Emperor Liang's Repentance ashram. Since the day he was sick in Uncle Mat's house, he has been chanting sutras day and night. Besides, he was a disciple of Venerable Hai Duc on a daily basis, and he recited Buddha's name a lot. I myself (the translator) have advised him to recite Buddha's name since 1954.

Buddhists take turns chanting until seven o'clock in the morning. He escaped peacefully as Buddha taught, with the testimony and protection of Venerable Thich Chanh Truc (Representing the Venerable), a strange scent filled the house. Everyone was happy, seeing something unprecedented.

As for his friend Hoi Xuan Duong, the Oriental medicine man who had been taking care of him for a long time, immediately developed the Bodhi mind, invited the statue to go to the Buddhist temple and worship. Narrative translator.

TEN MERITS OF THE INDIAN SONG SUTRA

1. If you have accidentally committed a crime, if the crime is light, it will be immediately extinguished; if the crime is serious, it will be changed to a light one. 2. Often supported by good gods, avoiding all pestilences, swordsmen, robbers, imprisonment, fire, drifting water, etc. 3. Thanks to the Dharma, those who were hostile to us in previous lives are freed, so they avoid the suffering of revenge. 4. Yaksha demons cannot invade, hungry tigers, and poisonous snakes cannot harm them. 5. The mind is at peace, there is no danger during the day, there are no nightmares at night, the beauty is bright and fresh, there is abundant energy, good deeds and benefits. 6. Wholeheartedly serve the Dharma, even though you do not expect anything, you will have enough food and clothing, and your family will be in harmony and blessed with eternal life. 7. In words and deeds, heaven and people are happy; Wherever he goes, he is admired by many people. 8. If you are stupid, you will become wise, if you are sick, you will become healthy, if you are in danger, you will become peaceful. If you are a woman, after death you will become a man. 9. Stay away from evil paths (hell, hungry ghosts, animals), and be born in good realms (human,

heavens), with a dignified appearance, intelligence, and exceptional blessings. 10. One gains the ability to nurture wholesome roots in other beings, taking their minds as a field of merit and reaping wholesome results. Wherever one is born, one can see the Buddha and hear the Dharma, develop the three kinds of wisdom arising from hearing, reflection, and practice, and attain the six higher knowledges: divine sight, divine hearing, knowledge of others' minds, spiritual powers, recollection of past lives, and the ending of the defilements. Printing and distributing sutras and sacred images brings such exceptional merit. Therefore, on occasions of wishing someone longevity, praying for peace, repentance, or dedicating merit to the deceased, one should gladly make an effort to print and distribute them.
